When a work order reading counts
A work order reading is recorded when the work order is invoiced, or when a service is marked complete on that work order, and only if someone entered or changed the value. The mileage a new work order copies from the asset is not a reading.
The estimate is replaced, not averaged
A recorded reading supersedes whatever was projected. The rate is then worked out again from the last three usable pairs of readings, read as one period, and the last reading is carried forward at that rate. At least two readings are needed for any estimate.
In the shop is not yet recorded
A unit on an open work order shows the value the advisor typed, dated today. The invoice is what fixes it.
Everything dependent moves at once
Due points, statuses and the worklist re-resolve on the save, not overnight. The one moment the truck is physically present is now.

One email, every state

Sent by hand

It holds for any mix
One service or several, all past due or all upcoming: the opening line never needs a singular and a plural version.
The state sits on the row
Not in the heading, not in the subject. The table carries it.
No unsubscribe
Honouring one properly is consent management, which is its own feature. Consent lives on the customer record instead.
